## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK
This verdict applies to G4 only. G5 is approve-with-changes. G4 uses a "tool block" as its unit and moves a result to the end of that block. A tool-only model response makes no `AssistantMessage`, so one block often holds several model responses. The result is that G4 does not fix the most common old-layout shapes for the OpenAI Chat and LiteLLM backends. G4 also changes ParallelAgent logs, which the spec says do not change, and in one interleaving it silently swaps tool results. The fixes are local: change the unit, the target position and the scope, and use the same rule in the test oracle.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
- **G4 "tool block" is the wrong unit, and "end of block" is the wrong target** - `build_items` makes an `AssistantMessage` only when the response has text or reasoning (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:517-529`). So two tool-only responses form one contiguous block. The OpenAI Chat translator starts a new `assistant{tool_calls}` message at each ToolCall that follows a `tool` message (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/translate/request.rs:54-79`). LiteLLM does the same (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/translate/request.rs:56-80`).
  - **Case 1: G4 moves the result, and the request is still invalid.** The child makes two tool-only rounds. The projection is `user, TC t, TC a, TR a, TC b, TR b, AM, TR t`. The spec output is `…TC b, TR b, TR t, AM`. On the wire this is `assistant[t,a], tool a, assistant[b], tool b, tool t`, and OpenAI rejects it because `t` has no response before the next assistant message.
  - **Case 2: G4 moves nothing.** The existing fixture `child_history_pairs_each_result_with_one_open_call` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:1034-1043`) projects to one block: `user, TC fc_0(t), TC fc_0(lookup), TR found, TC c1, TR cancelled`. G4 leaves it unchanged, and the wire is invalid.
  - **The spec contradicts itself.** Line 150 says "moves to the end of that block". T10 (line 295) says "moves to directly after the transfer call".
  - **The oracle cannot see the problem.** `assert_tool_calls_paired` also works at block level (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/deferred_resume.rs:579-611`, `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs:427-459`). T10 and T11 would pass on both invalid outputs.

  | Why it matters: G4 exists to make 0.6.0 sessions valid provider input. Tool-only responses are the normal shape for OpenAI and Gemini, and G4 fails on them without any test failing. | Suggested fix:
  - Define a "round" as a maximal run of ToolCall items plus the maximal run of ToolResult items directly after it.
  - A result is in place only when it is in its call's round.
  - Move a displaced result to directly after its call. This is the `close_open_transfers` rule (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/resume_exec.rs:182-185`), which the spec already accepts as valid input. With this rule, FIFO and LIFO give the same pairs afterwards.
  - Change the G3 projection check and `assert_tool_calls_paired` to the round rule: a ToolCall that comes after a ToolResult must find `outstanding` empty.
  - Add Case 1 and Case 2 to T10.

### MAJOR
- **LIFO runs on every log and swaps results under ParallelAgent with repeated ids** - ParallelAgent yields branch events interleaved (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/workflow.rs:377-420`). The Gemini fallback id starts again at `fc_0` for each stream (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:42-46`), so two Gemini branches both emit `fc_0`.
  - Take the log `AM(A), TC fc_0(search), AM(B), TC fc_0(lookup), TR(search data), TR(lookup data)`.
  - LIFO keeps `search data` after `lookup`. It moves `lookup data` to after `search`.
  - FIFO is correct for this interleaving. LIFO is correct for the opposite one.
  - The claim at spec lines 158-159 ("every log without a handoff projects as today") is false for ParallelAgent logs.

  | Why it matters: today this request is visibly malformed. After G4 it is well-formed, but each call has the other call's data, and nothing reports it. | Suggested fix: Move only results that pair with a transfer call. A transfer call is a `ToolCalled` in the run directly before a `HandoffOccurred` (the same scan as `transfer_calls_before`, `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:648-660`). `project()` iterates the events, so it can mark these calls. A minimum alternative: move a result only when exactly one open call has its id. Add a T10 case that an interleaved ParallelAgent log does not change.

- **Three pairing rules act on one history; the "no-op" claim is false** - These rules act on the same history:
  - The `project` repair: LIFO.
  - `paired_result`: FIFO (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/resume_exec.rs:199-219`).
  - The `agent_view` retain step: FIFO (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:606-621`).

  Take a same-id round with no text, `TC fc_0(t), TC fc_0(lookup), TR found, …, TR cancelled`. On the deny paths, `close_open_transfers` pairs `found` with `t` and moves it there, so the model sees `transfer → "found"`. LIFO was chosen to prevent exactly this pairing. For two transfer calls, the branch also moves results from the end of the block to `at+1`, so it is not a no-op (spec line 168). | Why it matters: two engineers will produce different histories, and the resume model request can still pair results wrongly. | Suggested fix: The "directly after its call" rule in the BLOCKER fix resolves this, because FIFO and LIFO then agree. State that, and add a test that runs `close_open_transfers` on a repaired same-id history with no text. Otherwise, use one private pairing helper for all three rules.

- **G5: ToolOutputItem is not the right lifetime boundary; state from sibling calls leaks into the child** - In a handoff response, `transition()` drops the non-transfer `ToolCallItem`s (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:303-315`). Their `ToolCallDelta`s already reached the mapper. These calls never get a ToolCallItem or a ToolOutputItem, so their `call_names`, `completed_calls` and `buffered_calls` entries stay. `TurnStarted` clears none of them (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs:133-142`). The child's Gemini stream uses `fc_0` and `fc_1` again. Three failures follow:
  - The child's START gets the sibling's name, because the name insert keeps the first value (`map.rs:164-168`).
  - A non-streamed child item is suppressed by `completed_calls` (`map.rs:226`).
  - The child's args are appended to the sibling's old buffer (`map.rs:195-196`). The flushed span then carries malformed JSON (`map.rs:214-225`).

  The ToolOutputItem arm reads neither map. A call's state is needed only between its first delta and its ToolCallItem, which is one model stream. | Why it matters: G5 does not fix the handoff case when the handoff response also holds a non-transfer call, and the spec's Non-goals line 62 says such calls exist. | Suggested fix: At `TurnStarted` (and/or `HandoffItem`), flush `buffered_calls` as complete spans (as `close_all` does, `map.rs:418-427`). Then clear `call_names` and `completed_calls`. State the ParallelAgent limit, as G3 does. Add a T12 case: handoff response `[search fc_0, transfer fc_1]`, then child response `[lookup fc_0, pay fc_1]`.

- **G5: a repeated toolCallId in one AG-UI run breaks the mapper's own client contract** - The module doc says "one call id maps to exactly one span" (`map.rs:23-25`). It also says that one call split across two spans "is exactly what breaks a client that keys state on toolCallId" (`map.rs:609-611`). `assert_tool_calls_well_formed` asserts one START per id (`map.rs:623-632`). G5 emits a second START, END and RESULT for `fc_0` in the same run, and the three-level G2 case emits three. A client that keys on the id merges these calls: it keeps the first name and joins the args. | Why it matters: the failure that G5 fixes in the mapper comes back in the client. T12 will also fail the existing helper, or someone will write it against the weaker nesting check. | Suggested fix: Give each call lifetime its own AG-UI id. The first use keeps the provider id; a reuse gets a suffix such as `fc_0~2`. Send `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` through the same table. AG-UI input drops `tool` messages (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore/src/agui/types.rs:47`), so no reverse mapping is needed. If raw ids stay, update the module doc, the field docs and the helper invariant, and add these to "Wording updates".

### MINOR
- **G5 id-uniqueness claim** - "Within one model stream a provider gives unique ids" is false for `ToolCallDelta`s with a blank id. The core contract says a provider must not merge them (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:190-197`). The claim is true at item level, because the accumulator merges by id (`model.rs:594`). Say "unique at item level". "A call's result always comes after its ToolCallItem" is also false for results in the resume window. That case is harmless because the mapper has no state for those ids.
- **G5: result for a buffered id** - A result can arrive for an id that is still in `buffered_calls` (ParallelAgent only). Removing its `call_names` entry makes the later flush show `"unknown"` (`map.rs:388-392`, `map.rs:418-423`). Specify that the arm takes the buffered entry first.
- **G4 implementation cost** - `project` runs on every snapshot and on every `CompactingSession` append (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/compacting_session.rs:147`, `:181`). Specify one O(n) pass that computes the targets and then rebuilds the list in order. Do not use repeated `Vec::remove`/`insert`.
- **G4 observability** - Add a `tracing::debug!` with the number of moved results, so an operator can see that an old session was repaired.

## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK
This verdict applies to G4 only. G5 is approve-with-changes. G4 uses a "tool block" as its unit and moves a result to the end of that block. A tool-only model response makes no `AssistantMessage`, so one block often holds several model responses. The result is that G4 does not fix the most common old-layout shapes for the OpenAI Chat and LiteLLM backends. G4 also changes ParallelAgent logs, which the spec says do not change, and in one interleaving it silently swaps tool results. The fixes are local: change the unit, the target position and the scope, and use the same rule in the test oracle.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
- **G4 "tool block" is the wrong unit, and "end of block" is the wrong target** - `build_items` makes an `AssistantMessage` only when the response has text or reasoning (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:517-529`). So two tool-only responses form one contiguous block. The OpenAI Chat translator starts a new `assistant{tool_calls}` message at each ToolCall that follows a `tool` message (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/translate/request.rs:54-79`). LiteLLM does the same (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/translate/request.rs:56-80`).
  - **Case 1: G4 moves the result, and the request is still invalid.** The child makes two tool-only rounds. The projection is `user, TC t, TC a, TR a, TC b, TR b, AM, TR t`. The spec output is `…TC b, TR b, TR t, AM`. On the wire this is `assistant[t,a], tool a, assistant[b], tool b, tool t`, and OpenAI rejects it because `t` has no response before the next assistant message.
  - **Case 2: G4 moves nothing.** The existing fixture `child_history_pairs_each_result_with_one_open_call` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:1034-1043`) projects to one block: `user, TC fc_0(t), TC fc_0(lookup), TR found, TC c1, TR cancelled`. G4 leaves it unchanged, and the wire is invalid.
  - **The spec contradicts itself.** Line 150 says "moves to the end of that block". T10 (line 295) says "moves to directly after the transfer call".
  - **The oracle cannot see the problem.** `assert_tool_calls_paired` also works at block level (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/deferred_resume.rs:579-611`, `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs:427-459`). T10 and T11 would pass on both invalid outputs.

  | Why it matters: G4 exists to make 0.6.0 sessions valid provider input. Tool-only responses are the normal shape for OpenAI and Gemini, and G4 fails on them without any test failing. | Suggested fix:
  - Define a "round" as a maximal run of ToolCall items plus the maximal run of ToolResult items directly after it.
  - A result is in place only when it is in its call's round.
  - Move a displaced result to directly after its call. This is the `close_open_transfers` rule (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/resume_exec.rs:182-185`), which the spec already accepts as valid input. With this rule, FIFO and LIFO give the same pairs afterwards.
  - Change the G3 projection check and `assert_tool_calls_paired` to the round rule: a ToolCall that comes after a ToolResult must find `outstanding` empty.
  - Add Case 1 and Case 2 to T10.

- **LIFO runs on every log and swaps results under ParallelAgent with repeated ids** - ParallelAgent yields branch events interleaved (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/workflow.rs:377-420`).   - Take the log `AM(A), TC fc_0(search), AM(B), TC fc_0(lookup), TR(search data), TR(lookup data)`.
  - LIFO keeps `search data` after `lookup`. It moves `lookup data` to after `search`.
  - FIFO is correct for this interleaving. LIFO is correct for the opposite one.

  | Why it matters: today this request is visibly malformed. After G4 it is well-formed, but each call has the other call's data, and nothing reports it. | Suggested fix: Move only results that pair with a transfer call. A transfer call is a `ToolCalled` in the run directly before a `HandoffOccurred` (the same scan as `transfer_calls_before`, `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-810/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:648-660`). `project()` iterates the events, so it can mark these calls. A call's state is needed only between its first delta and its ToolCallItem, which is one model stream. | Why it matters: G5 does not fix the handoff case when the handoff response also holds a non-transfer call, and the spec's Non-goals line 62 says such calls exist. | Suggested fix: At `TurnStarted` (and/or `HandoffItem`), flush `buffered_calls` as complete spans (as `close_all` does, `map.rs:418-427`).
